key_insight: A population-balance model can directly track pore-size evolution during freeze-drying microcollapse and link it to mass-transfer resistance with near-standard computational cost.
engineering_relevance: This gives process engineers a predictive way to model primary drying temperatures and resistance changes without relying solely on empirical post-hoc calibration or avoiding the microcollapse regime.
method: Model pore-size distribution with a population balance equation during drying.
Apply method-of-moments reduction with interpolative closure to keep computation lightweight.
Relate evolving pore size to mass-transfer resistance using a fitted rate constant.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful fits to literature data across high-, low-, and intermediate-temperature cases, plus agreement on product temperatures over multi-experiment conditions.
watch_item: The approach still needs parameter fitting and its accuracy may depend on formulation-specific microcollapse kinetics and the quality of available pore-size or temperature data.
paper_title: Direct Modeling of Pore Size Evolution and Microcollapse in Lyophilization by Population Balance
